study type: Real-world evidence registry study (descriptive subgroup analysis)
cohort: The study included 50 individuals from the RUBY registry who had preterm births less than 34 weeks gestational age and were treated with the Jada System for postpartum hemorrhage.
finding: The Jada System demonstrated high treatment success rates and a favorable safety profile for postpartum hemorrhage management in preterm births less than 34 weeks gestational age, including subgroups less than 28 wGA and 28 to less than 34 wGA, with results consistent with those for births 34 wGA or greater.
mod_finding: Treatment success rates were reported separately for vaginal and cesarean births within the preterm subgroups (e.g., 81.8% vaginal vs. 100% cesarean for <28 wGA; 100% vaginal vs. 82.6% cesarean for 28 to <34 wGA).
